  "limitations_stated": [
    "The study uses human TF and tPA for TG and PG measurements in distinct species samples, which presents a possible limitation.",
    "The rate of TF complex formation with factor VIIa (FVIIa) as well as activation of plasminogen by tPA can vary among different species, thus presenting limitation to hemostasis comparisons across species, in general.",
    "The total number of rabbits evaluated were relatively low."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "The authors state that they have no conflict of interest.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "TG and PG parameters can differ by more than 10 times across a range of species from rodents to humans.",
    "Human thrombin PH values were significantly greater than those from other primates.",
    "Plasmin PR from baboon plasmas was significantly greater than rhesus macaques.",
    "Thrombin PH and PR values did not differ between rat and swine plasmas.",
    "Rabbit and Guinea pig TG parameters were the lowest observed in the study.",
    "Guinea pig plasmin PR and PR values were the lowest in the study.",
    "In human samples the thrombin PH and PR values showed a significant correlation.",
    "In baboons, no correlation between thrombin PH and PR occurred, while significant correlation between PG parameters were detected.",
    "Rhesus macaque samples demonstrated correlations in both TG and PG parameters.",
    "In rat plasmas, TG parameters did not correlate while plasmin PH significantly correlated to plasmin PR.",
    "In rabbits, significant correlations in both TG and PG parameters were observed.",
    "Guinea pig samples showed significant correlation between TG and PG parameters.",
    "In swine, thrombin PH and PR values also significantly correlated.",
    "The correlations between coagulation (TG) and fibrinolysis (PG) parameters were generally weak for all the species evaluated.",
    "Human plasma samples: N=28",
    "Baboon plasma samples: N=10",
    "Rhesus macaque plasma samples: N=12",
    "Swine plasma samples: N=20",
    "Rat plasma samples: N=20",
    "Rabbit plasma samples: N=10",
    "Guinea pig plasma samples: N=14",
    "Two types of rabbit PG curves occurred.",
    "The first type of rabbit PG curves had high PR (6.21–85.36 nM/min, mean 33.94, SD 31.95).",
    "The second type of rabbit PG curves had low PR (0.65–2.65 nM/min, mean 1.32, SD 0.79).",
    "Swine plasma was not able to generate plasmin at the tPA concentration used in this study.",
    "Guinea pig plasmas demonstrated extremely low TG and the lowest PG activity of all species evaluated.",
    "The plasmin peaks in rats, guinea pigs and some rabbits were reached significantly later than in the samples of human and non-human primates."
  ]
